thread:
maria: FYI — automated canary shift to service-model v3.2.1 started and the rollout controller immediately auto-reverted to v3.2.0. release-bot shows health-check flapping and a "circuit_breaker" triggered. :eyes:
release-bot: [auto-rollback] rollout id=rl-2309 reason=unhealthy_traffic_surge metric=error_rate threshold=0.05 observed=0.12 action=rollback
sre-bot: [alert] spike in 429/503 from eu-west cluster during shift; correlated with k8s scheduling spikes and CNI "no IPs" logs.
ashok: I pulled the node and pod events — preStop hooks on model-worker pods are taking ~90s to finish because the GPU driver cleanup hangs when a pod is preempted. Readiness flips while connections close and the canary controller sees >5% errors. snippet:
```
# kubectl -n inference get events | tail -n 10
Normal  Killing    Pod model-worker-xyz  Container preStop hook  Took 90s
Warning BackOff     Pod model-worker-xyz  CrashLoopBackOff  Crash loop backoff
```

devon: Also seeing CNI/IPAM errors around the same window: some nodepools in eu-west hit IP allocation caps, causing pods to be scheduled onto stretched nodes which increased latency. From CNI logs:
```
E0312 02:11:23 ipam.go:312] no available IPs in subnet /26 for node ip-10-23-45-67
```

kevin: I checked the Helm values used by the rollout automation — circuitBreaker.threshold for the canary is set to 0.02 (2%) which is too tight for our bursty eval traffic. Suspect the controller legitimately tripped the breaker. Current values snippet:
```
canary:
  steps: [10, 30, 100]
  circuitBreaker:
    enabled: true
    threshold: 0.02
    windowSeconds: 60
```

lia: Proposal: 1) pause automated traffic ramp for the eu-west job, 2) temporarily increase circuitBreaker.threshold to 0.07 and windowSeconds to 120, 3) patch preStop to include a faster GPU-drain fallback (30s) to avoid long readiness flips, 4) run a controlled manual cutover once IPAM pressure confirmed resolved.
maria: Agree. Also let's avoid a full revert unless stable. I want a quick hotfix and a rollback plan pinned in the release ticket. Who can patch helm values and run the manual cut? :raised_hand:
ashok: I can patch the preStop and push a canary helm override. Command I'll run (one-off):
```
helm upgrade inference-service ./charts/inference -n inference --set canary.circuitBreaker.threshold=0.07 --set canary.circuitBreaker.windowSeconds=120 --set modelWorker.preStop.timeoutSeconds=30 --reuse-values
```

devon: I'll look at the IPAM quotas and scale the eu-west nodepool temporarily + open a quick PR to Terraform to increase subnet / add another /26. If Terraform workspace drift is the reason the autoscaler didn't create nodes, I'll reconcile.
kevin: Also let's change the rollout evaluation window in the controller from 60s->120s so transient blips don't trigger the breaker. I can make that config change in the rollout-controller chart.
lia: Note — this will increase cost for a few hours while we scale the nodepool; flagging in the ticket for cost ops approval.
maria: OK action items: ashok = preStop patch and helm override (now), devon = nodepool/subnet scale and TF reconcile, kevin = rollout-controller window change, lia = cost flag and coordinate manual shift. We'll keep automated rollback off for this job until green. Update ticket #REL-1421 with each step. :thumbsup:
kevin: quick followup — after patch we'll run a small 5% synthetic traffic blast to verify stability before continuing ramp.
sre-bot: [note] manual pause applied to rollout rl-2309 by maria; auto-rollback disabled for rl-2309 until 1767779000.
maria: Thanks team — try to keep messages short in the ticket, I'll triage any regressions.
